newsitem.title: TAIWAN: FORECAST-Taiwan Jan export orders - Reuters poll.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Taiwan Jan export orders - Reuters poll.

text.p: The following Reuters poll of Taiwan economists gives their projections for year-on-year growth for the island's export orders in January.
The figures are due to be released by the economics ministry at 0230 GMT on February 20.
Export orders in December rose 0.96 percent year-on-year.
The poll results produced an average forecast for a rise of 1.58 percent for annual export orders growth in January.
Economists said they expected relatively slow growth because of expected weak performance in the first quarter.

"Several major sectors, especially the electronics industry, will have stagnant growth in the first quarter and will not show an apparent sales rise in the second quarter," said Amy Huang of Nomura Securities, the most pessimistic economist polled.
Economists said they expected easing tensions between Taiwan and China to enable a gradual recovery in Taiwan-Hong Kong trade, which would contribute to the growth of overall orders received.
"We could expect a gradual rise, but not a major recovery, in orders from Hong Kong in January," said HSBC James Capel economist Stephen Wang.
